method: Five named sweeps (competitor set, UK bank set + v1.4 name-agnostic catch-alls, monetisation/trade press, experience & craft, region) plus editor-run verification fetches on every item that reached the shortlist. Publication dates were confirmed by fetching the source wherever the search snippet asserted a date; four apparently strong candidates were killed on date (Reward–Visa Europe = Aug 2020, RewardIQ = Sep 2025, Mastercard Commerce Media = Oct 2025, HSBC £500 Premier switch = 14 Apr 2026). Window note: Issue 2 declared 10 Jun – 10 Jul, so 1–10 July fell in its window but two significant items in that band (Visa's European agentic launch, 3 Jul; European Media Marketplace, 8 Jul) were not covered there. Issue 3 opens its window at 1 July to close that boundary gap rather than let it disappear; all such items carry their original date in the copy.

escalation_check.monetisation_lens: Not triggered. Issue 2's monetisation lens was the issue's lead trend (UK retail media). This issue's monetisation material is in-window and real (European Media Marketplace, 8 Jul). No two-thin-months escalation required.

candidates.title: Rezolve Ai embeds Reward's engagement platform in Zilch
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: A named competitor's card-linked-offer and commerce-media stack ships inside a payments app rather than a bank app — nearly 6m customers, $3.3bn a year of merchant flow. The distribution assumption the category was built on (the bank is the surface) is no longer the only one.
candidates.verified: Fetched primary release. Reward described as operating in 15+ markets across UK, Europe, ME and Asia; $2bn cashback returned to date, $4bn target by 2030.

candidates.title: Mastercard launches Wallet Services
candidates.region: Global (iOS first in US, UK, Europe)
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: SDKs, a Secure Element applet and MDES tokenisation let any bank, fintech or merchant put contactless payments in its own app without separate OS integrations or EMVCo certification — and Mastercard frames the new wallets explicitly as places to offer 'benefits, rewards, discounts, points'. More surfaces that can hold a payment credential means more surfaces that can hold a card-linked offer.
candidates.verified: Fetched. Chief Digital Officer Pablo Fourez quote confirmed. 200+ countries via MDES; first consumer products in select markets before end-2026.

candidates.title: Riyadh Air launches RX Pay with Saudi banks and Mastercard
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: An airline owns the loyalty brand and the earn currency; the banks issue. Sfeer Points now redeemable on any Mastercard purchase globally, not just flights. In the reader's GCC sales region, the bank is the rail rather than the programme owner.
candidates.verified: Fetched Zawya release (no explicit date on page; corroborated as July 2026 by Gulf Business, TradeArabia, Future Travel Experience). Multi-currency, split payment and instalments confirmed; phased rollout from Saudi Arabia under Mastercard exclusivity.

candidates.title: Visa completes live agent-driven purchases with 30+ European banks
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: Agents browsing, selecting and buying within user-defined parameters, live, with Barclays, HSBC UK, Lloyds, Nationwide, NatWest, Revolut and Klarna among 30+ banks, and lastminute.com, Frasers, Cleverbridge and BrickDepot as merchants. The reader's own bank customers are now on the agent rails — and no offer, reward or loyalty object appears anywhere in the announcement.
candidates.verified: Fetched. Payment Passkeys, Trusted Agent Protocol, Agent Directory; Cloudflare and Akamai supporting. Date 3 July 2026 (Issue 2's window, not covered there).

candidates.title: UCP's July state: identity linking made foundational, adoption tiny
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: The mechanism that makes a loyalty account visible to an agent is identity linking, and July's spec work put saved payment methods on the identity-linking infrastructure rather than a separate extension — identity is now the transactability layer. But identity capabilities are live at 15 stores, 99.7% of verified stores run one spec revision, and 0 of 11,414 verified stores expose payment capabilities.
candidates.verified: Fetched. Tracker-sourced figures, attributed as such in copy. Corroborated on direction by agenticplug.ai protocol tracker.

candidates.title: No loyalty-programme integrations or discount protocols announced in the period
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: Independent protocol tracker records identity linking as the loyalty-bearing capability in UCP and states that no prominent loyalty-programme integrations or dedicated discount protocols were announced in the period. Corroborates the gap rather than an assumption of one.
candidates.verified: Fetched. Also records x402 moving to Linux Foundation governance in July and MCP's 2026-07-28 spec.

candidates.title: Linux Foundation launches the x402 Foundation
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: Machine-to-machine payment standardisation moves to neutral governance with a 40-member coalition. Relevant as rails-hardening context; on its own it changes no offer decision. Also moving.
candidates.verified: Confirmed 14 July 2026 via Linux Foundation and Fintech Garden.

candidates.title: Visa Q3: value-added services positioned as a loyalty and engagement engine
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: Not the earnings number — the product substance behind it. VAS grew 34% to $3.8bn, near a third of revenue, and is being sold to banks as engagement: a Brazilian bank's World Cup promotion drew a million participants, an 8% card-activation lift and $400m of incremental payment volume; Visa Direct powers DoorDash's Crimson rewards-and-banking programme; a white-label AI financial assistant is being rolled out for issuer apps. The network is selling the engagement layer into the same budget the reader sells into.
candidates.verified: Fetched. Article 30 Jul reporting the 28 Jul call. Funding/valuation framing deliberately excluded per the double-reject gate.

candidates.title: Dotdigital Customer Trends Index and Dotdigital Loyalty launch
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: 4,000 consumers across four markets including the UK: 62% prefer points-based programmes, 53% free shipping, 52% cashback, 45% raised spend to reach a tier, 53% say loyalty programmes matter to a future brand relationship — but only 15% find the marketing they receive 'very relevant'. A martech platform ships a native loyalty product off the back of it.
candidates.verified: Fetched primary release, 16 July 2026. Censuswide fieldwork.

candidates.title: Eagle Eye's AI loyalty programme for Central Retail Vietnam passes 5.8m members
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: A specialist loyalty vendor's AI-personalised programme scaling fast in the reader's Asian footprint — evidence that the engagement layer is being bought as a service by large retailers, not only built.

candidates.title: European Media Marketplace launches, UK in the first five markets
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: Vinted, Deutsche Telekom's T Advertising Solutions, Equativ, Experian, lastminute.com, leboncoin, Kleinanzeigen, Orange Advertising, Virgin Media O2 and Vodafone build a cross-market alternative to closed ad ecosystems, spanning CTV, video, display, native and retail media. Issue 2's UK retail-media consolidation, one level up: pan-European and beyond retail. Campaigns from September 2026.
candidates.verified: Fetched Retail Gazette, 8 July 2026 (Issue 2's window, not covered there).

candidates.title: Visa Stablecoin Platform enters beta
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: Banks and fintechs can mint, hold, transfer and redeem stablecoins inside Visa's existing risk and settlement systems. Settlement infrastructure, not an offer surface — reference only this month.
candidates.verified: Confirmed 16 July 2026 across Finextra, Bloomberg, Fortune.

candidates.title: Mastercard examines a sale of Vocalink
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: UK payments infrastructure ownership in play. Structural, not a product decision this month — Also moving.

candidates.title: UK bank rewards: no new programme in the window
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: Recorded as quiet, not skipped. The full v1.3 bank sweep plus the v1.4 catch-alls returned no new UK bank rewards programme in the window: Lloyds Rewards continued to bed in with summer merchant offers, Chase's 2% behaviour-gated cashback took effect from 1 July as previously announced, and HSBC's £500 Premier switching incentive — which surfaced in July 'current offers' round-ups — was in fact announced 14 April 2026. Second consecutive quiet month for UK bank rewards launches.
candidates.verified: HSBC date checked against the bank's own newsroom and excluded from the trend set on that basis.

candidates.title: Cardlytics: Q2 results date and inducement grants
candidates.why_it_changes_a_product_decision: Nothing on its own — earnings scheduling and stock grants reject up. Recorded so the competitor is logged as quiet on product. Q2 results 5 August will be the first clean read after the Bank of America relationship ended (non-renewal completed February 2026).
candidates.verified: Confirmed via StockTitan and Cardlytics' 10-K coverage of the BofA exit.
